1.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. "The prophet Isaiah wrote" instead of "written in the prophets" in 1:2 and "the good news of God" instead of "the gospel of the kingdom of God" in 1:14), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V10 keeps the KJV 'opened' and explains it as 'torn open' (Greek schizomenous), the same word used for the temple veil at Jesus' death (15:38).

verses.text: The beginning of the gospel (good news) of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
As it is written in the prophets: Look, I send My messenger before Your face. He will prepare Your way before You.
The voice of one crying in the wilderness (desert): Prepare the way of the Lord. Make His paths straight.
John baptized in the wilderness (desert). John preached the baptism of repentance (a change of heart) for the remission (forgiveness) of sins.
All the land of Judaea went out to John, and the people of Jerusalem. They were all baptized by John in the river of Jordan, confessing (admitting) their sins.
John was clothed with camel's hair, and with a girdle (belt) of skin around his loins (waist). John ate locusts (grasshoppers) and wild honey.
John preached: One mightier than I comes after me. I am not worthy to stoop down and unloose (untie) the latchet (strap) of His shoes.
I indeed have baptized you with water. But He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.
In those days Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized by John in Jordan.
Right away, coming up out of the water, Jesus saw the heavens opened (torn open), and the Spirit like a dove descending (coming down) on Him.
A voice came from heaven: You are My beloved (dearly loved) Son, in whom I am well pleased.
Right away the Spirit drove Jesus into the wilderness (desert).
Jesus was there in the wilderness (desert) forty days, tempted by Satan. He was with the wild beasts. And the angels ministered to (served) Him.
After John was put in prison, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel (good news) of the kingdom of God.
Jesus said: The time is fulfilled (has come), and the kingdom of God is at hand (near). Repent (change your heart), and believe the gospel (good news).
As Jesus walked by the sea of Galilee, He saw Simon and Andrew his brother throwing a net into the sea. For they were fishers (fishermen).
Jesus said to them: Come after Me, and I will make you to become fishers of men (people who bring others to God).
Right away they forsook (left) their nets, and followed Jesus.
When Jesus had gone a little farther from there, He saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother. They were also in the ship (boat) mending (fixing) their nets.
Right away Jesus called them. They left their father Zebedee in the ship (boat) with the hired servants, and went after Jesus.
They went into Capernaum. Right away on the sabbath day (day of rest) Jesus entered into the synagogue (meeting house), and taught.
They were astonished (amazed) at His doctrine (teaching). For He taught them as one who had authority, and not as the scribes (teachers of the law).
In their synagogue (meeting house) there was a man with an unclean spirit. He cried out.
He said: Let us alone. What do we have to do with You, You Jesus of Nazareth? Have You come to destroy us? I know who You are, the Holy One of God.
Jesus rebuked (gave a strong command to) him. Jesus said: Hold your peace (be quiet), and come out of him.
When the unclean spirit had torn (shaken) the man, and cried with a loud voice, it came out of him.
They were all amazed. They questioned among themselves: What thing is this? What new doctrine (teaching) is this? For with authority He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him.
Right away His fame (news about Him) spread throughout all the region around Galilee.
Right away, when they had come out of the synagogue (meeting house), they entered into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
But Simon's wife's mother lay sick with a fever. Right away they told Jesus about her.
Jesus came and took her by the hand, and lifted her up. Right away the fever left her, and she ministered to (served) them.
At evening, when the sun set, they brought to Jesus all who were diseased (sick), and those who were possessed with devils (demons).
All the city was gathered together at the door.
Jesus healed many who were sick with divers (many different) diseases, and cast out (drove out) many devils (demons). He suffered (allowed) not the devils (demons) to speak, because they knew Him.
In the morning, rising up a great while before day, Jesus went out, and left for a solitary (lonely) place, and prayed there.
Simon and those who were with him followed after Jesus.
When they had found Him, they said to Him: All men seek (are looking) for You.
Jesus said to them: Let us go into the next towns, so I may preach there also. For that is why I came.
Jesus preached in their synagogues (meeting houses) throughout all Galilee, and cast out (drove out) devils (demons).
A leper (a man with a skin disease) came to Jesus, beseeching (begging) Him, and kneeling down to Him. He said to Jesus: If You will, You can make me clean.
Jesus, moved with compassion (deep pity), put out His hand, and touched him. Jesus said to him: I will. Be clean.
As soon as Jesus had spoken, right away the leprosy (skin disease) left him, and he was cleansed (healed).
Jesus straitly charged (strongly warned) him, and right away sent him away.

Jesus said to him: See that you say nothing to anyone. But go your way, show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing (healing) the things that Moses commanded, for a testimony (proof) to them.

But the man went out, and began to publish (tell) it much, and to blaze abroad (spread) the matter. So Jesus could no more openly enter into the city, but was without (outside) in desert places. And they came to Him from every quarter (direction).

2.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. leaving out "to repentance" in 2:17 and "and drinketh" in 2:16), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, with generic 'he' rendered gender-neutral in v21-22. V4 keeps the KJV 'uncovered the roof ... broken it up' (Greek exoryxantes, dug through).

verses.text: After some days Jesus entered into Capernaum again. And it was noised (told around) that He was in the house.
Right away many were gathered together, so that there was no room to receive them, no, not even around the door. And Jesus preached the word to them.
They came to Jesus, bringing a man sick with palsy (could not move his body). He was borne (carried) by four men.

When they could not come nigh (near) to Jesus because of the press (crowd), they uncovered the roof where He was. When they had broken it up, they let down the bed that the man sick with palsy (could not move his body) lay on.
When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the man sick with palsy (could not move his body): Son, your sins are forgiven you.
But some of the scribes (teachers of the law) were sitting there, and reasoning (thinking) in their hearts:
Why does this man speak blasphemies (words against God) like this? Who can forgive sins but God only?
Right away Jesus perceived (knew) in His spirit that they reasoned (thought) this within themselves. Jesus said to them: Why do you reason (think) these things in your hearts?
Which is easier, to say to the man sick with palsy (could not move his body): Your sins are forgiven you? Or to say: Arise (get up), and take up your bed, and walk?
But this is so that you may know that the Son of Man has power on earth to forgive sins. Then Jesus said to the man sick with palsy (could not move his body):
I say to you: Arise (get up), and take up your bed, and go your way into your house.
Right away the man arose (got up), took up the bed, and went out before them all. So they were all amazed, and glorified (praised) God. They said: We never saw anything like this.
Jesus went out again by the sea side. All the multitude (crowd) resorted (came) to Him, and He taught them.
As Jesus passed by, He saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the receipt of custom (tax booth). Jesus said to him: Follow Me. And Levi got up and followed Jesus.
As Jesus sat at meat (ate a meal) in Levi's house, many publicans (tax collectors) and sinners also sat together with Jesus and His disciples. For there were many, and they followed Jesus.

When the scribes (teachers of the law) and Pharisees saw Jesus eat with publicans (tax collectors) and sinners, they said to His disciples: How is it that He eats and drinks with publicans (tax collectors) and sinners?

When Jesus heard it, He said to them: Those who are whole (healthy) have no need of the physician (doctor), but those who are sick. I did not come to call the righteous (those who are right with God), but sinners to repentance (a change of heart).

The disciples of John and of the Pharisees used to fast (go without food). They came and said to Jesus: Why do the disciples of John and of the Pharisees fast (go without food), but Your disciples do not fast (go without food)?

Jesus said to them: Can the children of the bridechamber (friends of the bridegroom) fast (go without food) while the bridegroom (the man getting married) is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast (go without food).
But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them. Then they will fast (go without food) in those days.
No one sews a piece of new cloth on an old garment (piece of clothing). If they do, the new piece that filled it up pulls away from the old, and the rent (tear) is made worse.

No one puts new wine into old bottles (leather wine bags). If they do, the new wine bursts the bottles, and the wine is spilled, and the bottles will be marred (ruined). But new wine must be put into new bottles (leather wine bags).
Jesus went through the corn (grain) fields on the sabbath day (day of rest). As they went, His disciples began to pluck the ears of corn (heads of grain).
The Pharisees said to Jesus: Look, why do they do what is not lawful (allowed by the law) on the sabbath day (day of rest)?
Jesus said to them: Have you never read what David did when he had need, and was hungry, he and those who were with him?

David went into the house of God in the days of Abiathar the high priest. David ate the shewbread (holy bread set before God), which is not lawful (allowed by the law) to eat except for the priests. And he also gave some to those who were with him.
Jesus said to them: The sabbath (day of rest) was made for man, and not man for the sabbath (day of rest).
So the Son of Man is Lord also of the sabbath (day of rest).

3.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. leaving out "to heal sicknesses" in 3:15 and "whole as the other" in 3:5, adding "called them apostles" in 3:14, and "a sin that lasts forever" instead of "eternal damnation" in 3:29), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, with generic 'he/his' rendered gender-neutral in v27.

verses.text: Jesus entered again into the synagogue (meeting house). And there was a man there who had a withered (dried up and useless) hand.
They watched Jesus, whether He would heal the man on the sabbath day (day of rest), so that they might accuse Jesus.
Jesus said to the man who had the withered (dried up and useless) hand: Stand forth (stand up here).
Jesus said to them: Is it lawful (allowed by the law) to do good on the sabbath days, or to do evil? To save life, or to kill? But they held their peace (stayed quiet).

Jesus looked round about on them with anger, being grieved (very sad) for the hardness of their hearts. Jesus said to the man: Stretch out your hand. He stretched it out, and his hand was restored whole (healed) like the other.
The Pharisees went out, and right away took counsel (made plans) with the Herodians (followers of King Herod) against Jesus, how they might destroy Him.
But Jesus withdrew (went away) with His disciples to the sea. A great multitude (crowd) from Galilee followed Him, and from Judaea,
And from Jerusalem, and from Idumaea, and from beyond Jordan. And those around Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude (crowd), when they had heard what great things Jesus did, came to Him.
Jesus spoke to His disciples, that a small ship (boat) should wait for Him because of the multitude (crowd), or they would throng (crowd against) Him.
For Jesus had healed many. So they pressed upon Him to touch Him, as many as had plagues (sicknesses).
Unclean spirits, when they saw Jesus, fell down before Him, and cried out: You are the Son of God.
Jesus straitly charged (strongly warned) them that they should not make Him known.
Jesus went up into a mountain, and called to Him whoever He wanted. And they came to Him.
Jesus ordained (appointed) twelve, that they should be with Him, and that He might send them out to preach,
And to have power to heal sicknesses, and to cast out (drive out) devils (demons).
Simon He surnamed (gave the other name) Peter.
And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James. Jesus surnamed (gave the other name) them Boanerges, which means: The sons of thunder.
And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite,
And Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed (handed over) Jesus. And they went into a house.
The multitude (crowd) came together again, so that they could not even eat bread.
When His friends heard of it, they went out to lay hold on (take hold of) Him. For they said: He is beside Himself (out of His mind).
The scribes (teachers of the law) who came down from Jerusalem said: He has Beelzebub (the devil). And by the prince (ruler) of the devils (demons) He casts out (drives out) devils (demons).
Jesus called them to Him, and said to them in parables (stories that teach a lesson): How can Satan cast out (drive out) Satan?
If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
And if a house is divided against itself, that house cannot stand.
And if Satan rises up against himself, and is divided, he cannot stand, but has an end.
No one can enter into a strong man's house and spoil (steal) his goods, unless that person first binds (ties up) the strong man. Then that person will spoil (rob) his house.
Truly I say to you: All sins will be forgiven to the sons of men (people), and whatever blasphemies (words against God) they speak.
But whoever blasphemes (speaks against) the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation (punishment forever).
Because they said: He has an unclean spirit.
Then His brethren (brothers) and His mother came. Standing without (outside), they sent to Him, calling Him.
The multitude (crowd) sat around Him. They said to Him: Look, Your mother and Your brethren (brothers) are outside, looking for You.
Jesus answered them: Who is My mother, or My brethren (brothers)?
Jesus looked round about on those who sat around Him, and said: Look at My mother and My brethren (brothers)!
For whoever does the will of God, that person is My brother, and My sister, and mother.

4.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. "planted in them" instead of "sown in their hearts" in 4:15, dropping "so" fearful and "how is it" in 4:40, and adding "God will treat you" in 4:24), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. Parable characters (e.g. the farmer in v26-29) keep their 'he'.

verses.text: Jesus began again to teach by the sea side. A great multitude (crowd) was gathered to Him, so that He entered into a ship (boat), and sat in the sea. And the whole multitude was by the sea on the land.
Jesus taught them many things by parables (stories that teach a lesson). And He said to them in His doctrine (teaching):
Hearken (listen). Look, a sower (a man planting seed) went out to sow (plant seed).
As he sowed, some seed fell by the way side (along the path). The fowls (birds) of the air came and devoured (ate) it up.
Some fell on stony ground, where it did not have much earth (soil). Right away it sprang up, because it had no depth of earth (soil).
But when the sun was up, it was scorched (burned). And because it had no root, it withered (dried up) away.
Some fell among thorns. The thorns grew up and choked it, and it yielded (gave) no fruit.
Other seed fell on good ground. It yielded (gave) fruit that sprang up and increased. It brought forth (produced) some thirty, some sixty, and some a hundred.
Jesus said to them: Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.
When Jesus was alone, those who were around Him with the twelve asked Him about the parable (story that teaches a lesson).
Jesus said to them: To you it is given to know the mystery (secret) of the kingdom of God. But to those who are without (outside), all these things are done in parables (stories that teach a lesson).

So that seeing they may see, and not perceive (understand what they see). And hearing they may hear, and not understand. Otherwise they might be converted (turn back to God), and their sins would be forgiven them.
Jesus said to them: Do you not know this parable (story that teaches a lesson)? How then will you know all parables (stories that teach a lesson)?
The sower (the man planting seed) sows the word.
These are the ones by the way side (along the path), where the word is sown. When they have heard, Satan comes right away, and takes away the word that was sown in their hearts.
In the same way, these are the ones sown on stony ground. When they have heard the word, right away they receive it with gladness (joy).

But they have no root in themselves, and so endure (last) only for a time. Afterward, when affliction (trouble) or persecution (attack for faith) comes for the word's sake, right away they are offended (fall away).
These are the ones sown among thorns. They hear the word,
But the cares (worries) of this world, and the deceitfulness (lies) of riches, and the lusts (wrong desires) of other things come in and choke the word. And it becomes unfruitful (has no fruit).
These are the ones sown on good ground. They hear the word, and receive it, and bring forth (produce) fruit: some thirtyfold (30 times as much), some sixty, and some a hundred.
Jesus said to them: Is a candle (lamp) brought to be put under a bushel (basket), or under a bed? Is it not brought to be set on a candlestick (lamp stand)?
For there is nothing hidden that will not be manifested (shown). And nothing was kept secret, except that it should come abroad (out into the open).
If anyone has ears to hear, let them hear.
Jesus said to them: Take heed (be careful) what you hear. With the measure you mete (give out), it will be measured to you. And to you who hear, more will be given.
For whoever has, more will be given to them. And whoever does not have, even what they have will be taken from them.
Jesus said: The kingdom of God is like a man who throws seed into the ground.
He sleeps, and rises night and day. And the seed springs and grows up, he does not know how.
For the earth brings forth (produces) fruit by herself: first the blade (plant), then the ear (head of grain), after that the full corn (grain) in the ear.
But when the fruit is brought forth (ready), right away he puts in the sickle (curved knife for cutting grain), because the harvest has come.
Jesus said: What will we liken (compare) the kingdom of God to? Or with what comparison will we compare it?
It is like a grain of mustard seed. When it is sown in the earth, it is less (smaller) than all the seeds that are in the earth.
But when it is sown, it grows up, and becomes greater than all herbs (garden plants). It shoots out great branches, so that the fowls (birds) of the air may lodge (rest) under its shadow.
With many such parables (stories that teach a lesson) Jesus spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear it.
But without a parable (story that teaches a lesson) He did not speak to them. And when they were alone, Jesus expounded (explained) all things to His disciples.
The same day, when the evening had come, Jesus said to them: Let us pass over to the other side.
When they had sent away the multitude (crowd), they took Jesus just as He was in the ship (boat). And there were also other little ships (boats) with Him.
A great storm of wind arose. The waves beat into the ship (boat), so that it was now full.
Jesus was in the hinder part (back) of the ship (boat), asleep on a pillow. They woke Him, and said to Him: Master (Teacher), do You not care that we perish (are dying)?
Jesus arose (got up), and rebuked (gave a strong command to) the wind. Jesus said to the sea: Peace, be still. And the wind ceased (stopped), and there was a great calm.
Jesus said to them: Why are you so fearful? How is it that you have no faith?
They feared exceedingly (very much), and said to one another: What kind of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?

5.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. "Gerasenes" instead of "Gadarenes" in 5:1, dropping "all the devils" in 5:12 and "forthwith Jesus" in 5:13, and "paid no attention" instead of "as soon as Jesus heard" in 5:36), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. 5:30 'virtue' is explained as 'power' (Greek dunamis): the 1611 English word does not match the modern sign.

verses.text: They came over to the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gadarenes.
When Jesus had come out of the ship (boat), right away a man with an unclean spirit met Him, coming out of the tombs.
This man had his dwelling (home) among the tombs. No one could bind (tie up) him, no, not with chains.

For he had often been bound (tied up) with fetters (chains for the feet) and chains. But he had plucked the chains asunder (pulled the chains apart), and broken the fetters in pieces. No one could tame him.
Always, night and day, he was in the mountains, and in the tombs, crying out, and cutting himself with stones.
But when he saw Jesus afar off (from a distance), he ran and worshipped Him.
He cried with a loud voice: What do I have to do with You, Jesus, You Son of the most high God? I adjure (beg) You by God, do not torment (hurt) me.
For Jesus said to him: Come out of the man, you unclean spirit.
Jesus asked him: What is your name? He answered: My name is Legion (an army of thousands). For we are many.
He besought (begged) Jesus much that He would not send them away out of the country.
Now there was a great herd of swine (pigs) feeding there, nigh (near) to the mountains.
All the devils (demons) besought (begged) Jesus: Send us into the swine (pigs), so we may enter into them.

Right away Jesus gave them leave (permission). The unclean spirits went out, and entered into the swine (pigs). The herd ran violently down a steep place into the sea. (There were about two thousand.) And they were choked (drowned) in the sea.
Those who fed the swine (pigs) fled (ran away), and told it in the city, and in the country. And the people went out to see what had been done.
They came to Jesus. They saw the man who had been possessed with the devil (demon), and had the legion (army of demons), sitting, and clothed, and in his right mind. And they were afraid.
Those who saw it told them how it befell (happened) to the man who had been possessed with the devil (demon), and also about the swine (pigs).
They began to pray (beg) Jesus to leave their coasts (land).
When Jesus had come into the ship (boat), the man who had been possessed with the devil (demon) prayed (begged) Jesus that he might be with Him.
But Jesus suffered (allowed) him not. Jesus said to him: Go home to your friends, and tell them how great things the Lord has done for you, and how He has had compassion (deep pity) on you.
The man left, and began to publish (tell) in Decapolis (the Ten Cities) how great things Jesus had done for him. And all men did marvel (were amazed).
When Jesus had passed over again by ship (boat) to the other side, many people gathered to Him. And He was nigh (near) to the sea.
And look, one of the rulers of the synagogue (meeting house) came, named Jairus. When he saw Jesus, he fell at His feet.
Jairus besought (begged) Jesus greatly: My little daughter lies at the point of death. I pray (beg) You, come and lay Your hands on her, so that she may be healed. And she will live.
Jesus went with him. Many people followed Jesus, and thronged (crowded against) Him.
A certain woman had an issue of blood (bleeding) for twelve years.
She had suffered many things from many physicians (doctors), and had spent all that she had. She was nothing bettered (not any better), but instead grew worse.
When she had heard of Jesus, she came in the press (crowd) behind Him, and touched His garment (clothes).
For she said: If I may touch only His clothes, I will be whole (healed).
Right away the fountain (flow) of her blood was dried up. And she felt in her body that she was healed of that plague (sickness).
Right away Jesus knew in Himself that virtue (power) had gone out of Him. Jesus turned around in the press (crowd), and said: Who touched My clothes?
His disciples said to Him: You see the multitude (crowd) thronging (crowding against) You, and You say: Who touched Me?
Jesus looked round about to see her who had done this thing.
But the woman, fearing and trembling, knowing what was done in her, came and fell down before Jesus, and told Him all the truth.
Jesus said to her: Daughter, your faith has made you whole (healed). Go in peace, and be whole (healed) of your plague (sickness).
While Jesus was still speaking, some people came from the house of the ruler of the synagogue (meeting house). They said: Your daughter is dead. Why do you trouble the Master (Teacher) any further?
As soon as Jesus heard the word that was spoken, He said to the ruler of the synagogue (meeting house): Do not be afraid. Only believe.
Jesus suffered (allowed) no one to follow Him, except Peter, and James, and John the brother of James.
Jesus came to the house of the ruler of the synagogue (meeting house). He saw the tumult (noise and confusion), and those who wept and wailed (cried loudly) greatly.
When Jesus had come in, He said to them: Why do you make this ado (noisy fuss), and weep? The damsel (girl) is not dead, but sleeps.

They laughed Him to scorn (laughed at Him). But when Jesus had put them all out, He took the father and the mother of the damsel (girl), and those who were with Him, and entered in where the damsel (girl) was lying.
Jesus took the damsel (girl) by the hand, and said to her: Talitha cumi. That means: Damsel (girl), I say to you, arise (get up).
Right away the damsel (girl) arose (got up), and walked. For she was twelve years old. And they were astonished (amazed) with a great astonishment (amazement).
Jesus charged them straitly (strongly warned them) that no one should know it. And He commanded that something should be given to her to eat.

6.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. dropping the Sodom and Gomorrha sentence in 6:11, "some people were saying" instead of "he said" in 6:14, and "it troubled him" instead of "he did many things" in 6:20), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, with generic 'his' rendered gender-neutral in v4. V43 keeps the KJV word 'baskets' explained as small hand-baskets (kophinoi), matching Matthew 14:20. V48 keeps 'the fourth watch of the night' (between 3 and 6 in the morning).

verses.text: Jesus went out from there, and came into His own country (hometown). And His disciples followed Him.

When the sabbath day (day of rest) had come, Jesus began to teach in the synagogue (meeting house). Many hearing Him were astonished (amazed). They said: Where did this man get these things? What wisdom is this that is given to Him, that even such mighty works are wrought (done) by His hands?
Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? And are not His sisters here with us? And they were offended at Him (turned away from Him).
But Jesus said to them: A prophet is not without honour (respect), except in that prophet's own country (hometown), and among that prophet's own kin (relatives), and in that prophet's own house.
Jesus could do no mighty work there, except that He laid His hands on a few sick folk (people), and healed them.
Jesus marvelled (was amazed) because of their unbelief. And He went round about the villages, teaching.
Jesus called the twelve to Him. He began to send them out two by two. And He gave them power over unclean spirits.
Jesus commanded them to take nothing for their journey, except a staff (walking stick) only. No scrip (traveling bag), no bread, no money in their purse (money belt).
But be shod (wear) sandals, and do not put on two coats.
Jesus said to them: In whatever place you enter into a house, abide (stay) there until you leave that place.

Whoever will not receive you, or hear you, when you leave there, shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony (proof) against them. Truly I say to you: It will be more tolerable (easier) for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment than for that city.
They went out, and preached that men should repent (change their hearts).
They cast out (drove out) many devils (demons), and anointed (put oil on) many who were sick, and healed them.
King Herod heard of Jesus, for His name was spread abroad (everywhere). Herod said: John the Baptist is risen from the dead. That is why mighty works show themselves in him.
Others said: It is Elias (Elijah). And others said: It is a prophet, or like one of the prophets.
But when Herod heard of it, he said: It is John, whom I beheaded (cut off the head of). He is risen from the dead.
For Herod himself had sent out and laid hold (taken hold) of John, and bound (tied) him in prison. Herod did this for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife. For Herod had married her.
For John had said to Herod: It is not lawful (allowed by the law) for you to have your brother's wife.
So Herodias had a quarrel (grudge) against John, and wanted to kill him. But she could not.
For Herod feared John, knowing that he was a just (good and innocent) man and a holy man. Herod observed (protected) him. When Herod heard John, he did many things, and heard him gladly.
Then a convenient (good) day came. Herod on his birthday made a supper for his lords (nobles), high captains (army officers), and chief estates (leading men) of Galilee.
The daughter of Herodias came in and danced. She pleased Herod and those who sat with him. The king said to the damsel (girl): Ask me whatever you want, and I will give it to you.
Herod sware (made a promise to God) to her: Whatever you ask of me, I will give it to you, up to half of my kingdom.
She went out, and said to her mother: What will I ask? Her mother said: The head of John the Baptist.
Right away she came in with haste (hurry) to the king, and asked: I want you to give me by and by (right now) in a charger (large platter) the head of John the Baptist.
The king was exceeding (very) sorry. Yet for his oath's (promise's) sake, and for the sake of those who sat with him, he would not reject (refuse) her.
Right away the king sent an executioner (a man who kills prisoners), and commanded John's head to be brought. He went and beheaded (cut off the head of) John in the prison.
He brought John's head in a charger (large platter), and gave it to the damsel (girl). And the damsel (girl) gave it to her mother.
When John's disciples heard of it, they came and took up his corpse (dead body), and laid it in a tomb.
The apostles (sent ones) gathered together to Jesus. They told Him all things, both what they had done, and what they had taught.
Jesus said to them: Come apart (away) by yourselves into a desert place, and rest a while. For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure (free time) even to eat.
They left by ship (boat) privately into a desert place.
The people saw them leaving, and many knew Jesus. They ran afoot (on foot) there out of all cities, and outwent (got there before) them, and came together to Jesus.
When Jesus came out, He saw many people. He was moved with compassion (deep pity) toward them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. And He began to teach them many things.
When the day was now far spent (almost over), His disciples came to Jesus. They said: This is a desert place, and now the time is far passed (late).
Send them away, so they may go into the country around, and into the villages, and buy themselves bread. For they have nothing to eat.
Jesus answered them: You give them something to eat. They said to Jesus: Will we go and buy two hundred pennyworth (two hundred days' pay) of bread, and give them to eat?
Jesus said to them: How many loaves (of bread) do you have? Go and see. When they knew, they said: Five, and two fishes.
Jesus commanded them to make all sit down by companies (groups) on the green grass.
They sat down in ranks (rows), by hundreds, and by fifties.

When Jesus had taken the five loaves and the two fishes, He looked up to heaven, and blessed, and broke the loaves. He gave them to His disciples to set before the people. And He divided the two fishes among them all.
They all ate, and were filled.
They took up twelve baskets (small hand-baskets) full of the fragments (pieces), and of the fishes.
Those who ate of the loaves were about five thousand men.
Right away Jesus constrained (made) His disciples get into the ship (boat), and go before Him to the other side to Bethsaida, while He sent away the people.
When Jesus had sent them away, He went into a mountain to pray.
When evening came, the ship (boat) was in the middle of the sea, and Jesus was alone on the land.

Jesus saw them toiling (working hard) in rowing, for the wind was contrary (blowing against them). About the fourth watch of the night (between 3 and 6 in the morning) He came to them, walking on the sea, and would have passed by them.
But when they saw Jesus walking on the sea, they supposed (thought) it was a spirit (ghost), and cried out.
For they all saw Him, and were troubled (afraid). Right away Jesus talked with them. He said to them: Be of good cheer (take heart). It is I. Do not be afraid.
Jesus went up to them into the ship (boat), and the wind ceased (stopped). They were sore (very) amazed in themselves beyond measure, and wondered.
For they did not consider (understand) the miracle of the loaves. For their heart was hardened.
When they had passed over, they came into the land of Gennesaret, and drew to the shore.
When they had come out of the ship (boat), right away the people knew Jesus.
They ran through that whole region around, and began to carry around in beds those who were sick, to where they heard Jesus was.

Wherever Jesus entered, into villages, or cities, or country, they laid the sick in the streets. They besought (begged) Him that they might touch even the border (edge) of His garment (clothes). And as many as touched Him were made whole (healed).

7.source: Rewritten 2026-11-21 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. dropping "they found fault" in 7:2 and "as the washing of pots and cups" in 7:8, "Tyre" alone in 7:24, "through Sidon" in 7:31, and adding "Jesus made all foods clean" in 7:19), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, with generic 'he/him' rendered gender-neutral in v10-12, v15-23. V32-37 (the healing of the deaf man) keep the KJV words plainly: deaf, speech, dumb (could not speak).

verses.text: Then the Pharisees, and some of the scribes (teachers of the law) who came from Jerusalem, came together to Jesus.
They saw some of His disciples eat bread with defiled (unclean), that is to say, with unwashen (unwashed) hands. And they found fault.
For the Pharisees, and all the Jews, do not eat unless they wash their hands oft (carefully). They hold (keep) the tradition (handed-down rules) of the elders.

When they come from the market, they do not eat unless they wash. And there are many other things they have received to hold (keep), like the washing of cups, and pots, brasen vessels (brass pots), and tables.

Then the Pharisees and scribes (teachers of the law) asked Jesus: Why do Your disciples not walk (live) by the tradition (handed-down rules) of the elders, but eat bread with unwashen (unwashed) hands?

Jesus answered them: Esaias (Isaiah) prophesied (spoke God's message) well about you hypocrites (pretenders), as it is written: This people honours (respects) Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me.
But in vain (for nothing) they worship Me, teaching for doctrines (teachings) the commandments of men.
For laying aside the commandment of God, you hold (keep) the tradition (handed-down rules) of men, like the washing of pots and cups. And many other such things you do.
Jesus said to them: Full well (very cleverly) you reject the commandment of God, so that you may keep your own tradition (handed-down rules).
For Moses said: Honour (respect) your father and your mother. And: Whoever curses father or mother, let that person die the death (surely be put to death).
But you say: If anyone says to their father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift (given to God), whatever you might have been helped by from me, that person will be free.
And you suffer (allow) that person no more to do anything for their father or their mother.
You make the word of God of none effect (worthless) through your tradition (handed-down rules), which you have delivered (passed down). And you do many such things.
When Jesus had called all the people to Him, He said to them: Hearken (listen) to Me, every one of you, and understand.
There is nothing from without (outside) a person that can defile (make unclean) them by entering into them. But the things that come out of a person, those are what defile (make unclean) the person.
If anyone has ears to hear, let them hear.
When Jesus had entered into the house away from the people, His disciples asked Him about the parable (story that teaches a lesson).
Jesus said to them: Are you also so without understanding? Do you not perceive (understand) that whatever enters into a person from without (outside) cannot defile (make unclean) them?
Because it does not enter into the heart, but into the belly (stomach), and goes out into the draught (toilet), purging (cleaning out) all meats (foods).
Jesus said: What comes out of a person, that defiles (makes unclean) the person.
For from within, out of the heart of men, come evil thoughts, adulteries (being unfaithful in marriage), fornications (sexual sins), murders,

Thefts, covetousness (wanting what belongs to others), wickedness, deceit (lying), lasciviousness (shameless sexual desire), an evil eye (jealousy), blasphemy (speaking against God), pride, foolishness.
All these evil things come from within, and defile (make unclean) the person.
Jesus arose (got up) and went from there into the borders of Tyre and Sidon. He entered into a house, and wanted no one to know it. But He could not be hid.
For a certain woman, whose young daughter had an unclean spirit, heard of Jesus. She came and fell at His feet.
The woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician (from Phoenicia in Syria) by nation. She besought (begged) Jesus to cast out (drive out) the devil (demon) from her daughter.
But Jesus said to her: Let the children first be filled. For it is not meet (right) to take the children's bread, and throw it to the dogs.
She answered Him: Yes, Lord. Yet the dogs under the table eat of the children's crumbs.
Jesus said to her: For this saying, go your way. The devil (demon) has gone out of your daughter.
When she had come to her house, she found the devil (demon) gone out, and her daughter laid on the bed.
Again, leaving the coasts (land) of Tyre and Sidon, Jesus came to the sea of Galilee, through the middle of the coasts (land) of Decapolis (the Ten Cities).
They brought to Jesus a man who was deaf, and had an impediment (problem) in his speech. They besought (begged) Jesus to put His hand on him.
Jesus took him aside from the multitude (crowd). He put His fingers into the man's ears. He spit, and touched the man's tongue.
Looking up to heaven, Jesus sighed, and said to him: Ephphatha. That means: Be opened.
Right away the man's ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed (set free), and he spoke plain (clearly).
Jesus charged (strongly told) them to tell no one. But the more He charged them, so much the more they published (told) it.
They were beyond measure astonished (amazed). They said: He has done all things well. He makes both the deaf to hear, and the dumb (those who could not speak) to speak.

8.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text in places, e.g. dropping "nor tell it to any in the town" in 8:26, and it added words not in the KJV in 8:38 such as 'that coward'), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, with generic 'he/his/him' rendered gender-neutral in v34-38. V8, 19-20 keep the KJV word 'baskets' with the small hand-baskets (5,000) / large hampers (4,000) distinction, matching Matthew 16:9-10.

verses.text: In those days the multitude (crowd) was very great, and had nothing to eat. Jesus called His disciples to Him, and said to them:
I have compassion (deep pity) on the multitude (crowd), because they have now been with Me three days, and have nothing to eat.
If I send them away fasting (without food) to their own houses, they will faint (pass out) on the way. For divers (some) of them came from far.
His disciples answered Him: Where could anyone get enough bread here in the wilderness (desert) to satisfy (fill) these men?
Jesus asked them: How many loaves (of bread) do you have? They said: Seven.

Jesus commanded the people to sit down on the ground. He took the seven loaves, and gave thanks, and broke them. He gave them to His disciples to set before the people. And they set them before the people.
They had a few small fishes. Jesus blessed them, and commanded to set them also before the people.
So they ate, and were filled. They took up seven baskets (large hampers) of the broken meat (leftover food) that was left.
Those who had eaten were about four thousand. And Jesus sent them away.
Right away Jesus entered into a ship (boat) with His disciples, and came into the parts of Dalmanutha.
The Pharisees came out, and began to question with Him. They sought (asked) from Him a sign from heaven, tempting (testing) Him.
Jesus sighed deeply in His spirit, and said: Why does this generation (people living now) seek after a sign? Truly I say to you: No sign will be given to this generation.
Jesus left them, and entering into the ship (boat) again, went to the other side.
Now the disciples had forgotten to take bread. They did not have more than one loaf with them in the ship (boat).
Jesus charged (strongly told) them: Take heed (be careful). Beware of the leaven (yeast) of the Pharisees, and of the leaven (yeast) of Herod.
They reasoned (talked it over) among themselves. They said: It is because we have no bread.
When Jesus knew it, He said to them: Why do you reason (talk it over), because you have no bread? Do you not yet perceive (see), or understand? Is your heart still hardened?
Having eyes, do you not see? And having ears, do you not hear? And do you not remember?
When I broke the five loaves among five thousand, how many baskets (small hand-baskets) full of fragments (pieces) did you take up? They said to Him: Twelve.
And when I broke the seven among four thousand, how many baskets (large hampers) full of fragments (pieces) did you take up? They said: Seven.
Jesus said to them: How is it that you do not understand?
Jesus came to Bethsaida. They brought a blind man to Him, and besought (begged) Him to touch him.
Jesus took the blind man by the hand, and led him out of the town. When He had spit on the man's eyes, and put His hands on him, Jesus asked him if he saw anything.
The man looked up, and said: I see men like trees, walking.
After that Jesus put His hands again on the man's eyes, and made him look up. He was restored (healed), and saw every man clearly.
Jesus sent him away to his house. Jesus said: Do not go into the town, and do not tell it to anyone in the town.
Jesus went out with His disciples into the towns of Caesarea Philippi. On the way He asked His disciples: Who do men say that I am?
They answered: John the Baptist. But some say Elias (Elijah). And others say one of the prophets.
Jesus said to them: But who do you say that I am? Peter answered Him: You are the Christ.
Jesus charged (strongly told) them to tell no one about Him.

Jesus began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things. He must be rejected by the elders, and by the chief priests, and scribes (teachers of the law), and be killed, and after three days rise again.
Jesus spoke that saying openly. And Peter took Him aside, and began to rebuke (scold) Him.
But when Jesus had turned around and looked at His disciples, He rebuked (scolded) Peter. Jesus said: Get behind Me, Satan. For you savour (care about) not the things of God, but the things of men.
When Jesus had called the people to Him with His disciples also, He said to them: Whoever will come after Me, let them deny themselves (say no to self), and take up their cross, and follow Me.
For whoever will save their life will lose it. But whoever loses their life for My sake and the gospel's (good news'), that person will save it.
For what will it profit (help) a person, if they gain the whole world, and lose their own soul?
Or what will a person give in exchange for their soul?

So whoever is ashamed of Me and of My words in this adulterous (unfaithful to God) and sinful generation (people living now), of that person the Son of Man will also be ashamed, when He comes in the glory of His Father with the holy angels.

9.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. dropping "and fasting" in 9:29, "Lord" and "with tears" in 9:24, and "believe" in 9:23 ("If you can?")), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, with generic 'he/his' rendered gender-neutral in v35, v41-42. V44 and v46 are kept (modern Bibles drop them). 'Hell' in v43-47 is Gehenna and stays 'hell'.

verses.text: Jesus said to them: Truly I say to you: There are some of those standing here who will not taste of death (die), until they have seen the kingdom of God come with power.
After six days Jesus took with Him Peter, and James, and John, and led them up into a high mountain, apart by themselves. And He was transfigured (changed in appearance) before them.
His raiment (clothes) became shining, exceeding (very) white as snow, whiter than any fuller (cloth cleaner) on earth could make them.
Elias (Elijah) with Moses appeared to them. And they were talking with Jesus.
Peter answered Jesus: Master (Teacher), it is good for us to be here. Let us make three tabernacles (tents): one for You, and one for Moses, and one for Elias (Elijah).
For Peter wist (knew) not what to say, for they were sore (very) afraid.
A cloud overshadowed (covered) them. And a voice came out of the cloud: This is My beloved (dearly loved) Son. Hear Him.
Suddenly, when they had looked round about, they saw no one any more, except Jesus only with themselves.
As they came down from the mountain, Jesus charged (strongly told) them to tell no one what things they had seen, until the Son of Man was risen from the dead.
They kept that saying with themselves, questioning one with another what the rising from the dead should mean.
They asked Jesus: Why do the scribes (teachers of the law) say that Elias (Elijah) must come first?

Jesus answered them: Elias (Elijah) truly comes first, and restores (makes right again) all things. And it is written of the Son of Man that He must suffer many things, and be set at nought (treated as nothing).
But I say to you: Elias (Elijah) has indeed come, and they have done to him whatever they listed (wanted), as it is written about him.
When Jesus came to His disciples, He saw a great multitude (crowd) around them, and the scribes (teachers of the law) questioning with them.
Right away all the people, when they beheld (saw) Jesus, were greatly amazed. And running to Him, they saluted (greeted) Him.
Jesus asked the scribes (teachers of the law): What are you questioning with them?
One of the multitude (crowd) answered: Master (Teacher), I have brought my son to You. He has a dumb spirit (a spirit that keeps him from speaking).

Wherever it takes him, it tears (throws) him down. He foams, and gnashes (grinds) his teeth, and pines away (wastes away). I spoke to Your disciples, that they should cast it out (drive it out). And they could not.
Jesus answered him: O faithless generation (people living now), how long will I be with you? How long will I suffer (put up with) you? Bring him to Me.
They brought the boy to Jesus. When the spirit saw Jesus, right away it tore (threw) the boy. He fell on the ground, and wallowed (rolled around), foaming.
Jesus asked his father: How long is it since this came to him? The father said: Of a child (since he was a child).
Ofttimes (often) it has thrown him into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him. But if You can do anything, have compassion (deep pity) on us, and help us.
Jesus said to him: If you can believe, all things are possible to the one who believes.
Right away the father of the child cried out, and said with tears: Lord, I believe. Help my unbelief.

When Jesus saw that the people came running together, He rebuked (gave a strong command to) the foul (evil) spirit. Jesus said to it: You dumb and deaf spirit (spirit that keeps him from speaking and hearing), I charge (command) you, come out of him, and enter no more into him.
The spirit cried out, and rent him sore (shook him hard), and came out of him. The boy was like one dead, so that many said: He is dead.
But Jesus took him by the hand, and lifted him up. And he arose (got up).
When Jesus had come into the house, His disciples asked Him privately: Why could we not cast it out (drive it out)?
Jesus said to them: This kind can come out by nothing, except by prayer and fasting (going without food).
They left there, and passed through Galilee. And Jesus did not want anyone to know it.
For Jesus taught His disciples, and said to them: The Son of Man is delivered (handed over) into the hands of men, and they will kill Him. After He is killed, He will rise the third day.
But they did not understand that saying, and were afraid to ask Him.
Jesus came to Capernaum. Being in the house, He asked them: What was it that you disputed (argued) among yourselves on the way?
But they held their peace (stayed quiet). For on the way they had disputed (argued) among themselves who would be the greatest.
Jesus sat down, and called the twelve. He said to them: If anyone desires (wants) to be first, that person will be last of all, and servant of all.
Jesus took a child, and set the child in the middle of them. When He had taken the child in His arms, He said to them:
Whoever receives one of such children in My name receives Me. And whoever receives Me receives not Me, but the One who sent Me.
John answered Jesus: Master (Teacher), we saw someone casting out (driving out) devils (demons) in Your name, and he does not follow us. And we forbad (stopped) him, because he does not follow us.
But Jesus said: Forbid him not (do not stop him). For there is no one who will do a miracle in My name, who can lightly (quickly) speak evil of Me.
For whoever is not against us is on our part (side).
For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink in My name, because you belong to Christ, truly I say to you: That person will not lose their reward.

Whoever offends (causes to sin) one of these little ones who believe in Me, it is better for that person that a millstone (large heavy stone) were hung around their neck, and they were thrown into the sea.

If your hand offends you (causes you to sin), cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life maimed (missing a body part), than having two hands to go into hell, into the fire that never will be quenched (put out).
Where their worm does not die, and the fire is not quenched (put out).

If your foot offends you (causes you to sin), cut it off. It is better for you to enter halt (crippled) into life, than having two feet to be thrown into hell, into the fire that never will be quenched (put out).
Where their worm does not die, and the fire is not quenched (put out).
If your eye offends you (causes you to sin), pluck it out. It is better for you to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye, than having two eyes to be thrown into hell fire.
Where their worm does not die, and the fire is not quenched (put out).
For every one will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be salted with salt.
Salt is good. But if the salt has lost its saltness (salty taste), with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and have peace one with another.

10.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. dropping "take up the cross" in 10:21 and "for them that trust in riches" in 10:24), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, with generic 'he' rendered gender-neutral in v15, v29-30, v43-44.

verses.text: Jesus arose (got up) and went from there into the coasts (land) of Judaea, by the farther side of Jordan. The people resort (came) to Him again. And as He was wont (used to), He taught them again.
The Pharisees came to Jesus, and asked Him: Is it lawful (allowed by the law) for a man to put away (divorce) his wife? They asked this tempting (testing) Him.
Jesus answered them: What did Moses command you?
They said: Moses suffered (allowed) a man to write a bill of divorcement (written divorce paper), and to put her away (divorce her).
Jesus answered them: For the hardness of your heart Moses wrote you this precept (rule).
But from the beginning of the creation God made them male and female.
For this cause a man will leave his father and mother, and cleave (hold tight) to his wife.
And they twain (two) will be one flesh. So then they are no more twain (two), but one flesh.
So what God has joined together, let not man put asunder (pull apart).
In the house His disciples asked Him again about the same matter.
Jesus said to them: Whoever puts away (divorces) his wife, and marries another, commits adultery against her.
And if a woman puts away (divorces) her husband, and is married to another, she commits adultery.
They brought young children to Jesus, so that He would touch them. And His disciples rebuked (scolded) those who brought them.
But when Jesus saw it, He was much displeased. Jesus said to them: Suffer (allow) the little children to come to Me, and forbid them not (do not stop them). For of such is the kingdom of God.
Truly I say to you: Whoever will not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will not enter into it.
Jesus took them up in His arms, put His hands on them, and blessed them.
When Jesus had gone out into the way (road), a man came running, and kneeled to Him. He asked Jesus: Good Master (Teacher), what will I do so that I may inherit (receive) eternal life?
Jesus said to him: Why do you call Me good? There is none good but one, that is, God.

You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery (be unfaithful in marriage). Do not kill. Do not steal. Do not bear false witness (lie about others). Defraud (cheat) not. Honour (respect) your father and mother.
He answered Jesus: Master (Teacher), all these I have observed (kept) from my youth (since I was young).

Then Jesus beholding (looking at) him loved him. Jesus said to him: One thing you lack (still need). Go your way. Sell whatever you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. And come, take up the cross, and follow Me.
He was sad at that saying, and went away grieved (very sad). For he had great possessions (many things he owned).
Jesus looked round about, and said to His disciples: How hardly (with great difficulty) will those who have riches enter into the kingdom of God!
The disciples were astonished (amazed) at His words. But Jesus answered again, and said to them: Children, how hard it is for those who trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of God!
It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
They were astonished (amazed) out of measure (beyond words). They said among themselves: Who then can be saved?
Jesus looking at them said: With men it is impossible, but not with God. For with God all things are possible.
Then Peter began to say to Jesus: Lo (look), we have left all, and have followed You.

Jesus answered: Truly I say to you: There is no one who has left house, or brethren (brothers), or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for My sake, and the gospel's (good news'),

But that person will receive a hundredfold (100 times as much) now in this time: houses, and brethren (brothers), and sisters, and mothers, and children, and lands, with persecutions (attacks for faith). And in the world to come, eternal life.
But many who are first will be last, and the last first.

They were on the way going up to Jerusalem. Jesus went before them, and they were amazed. As they followed, they were afraid. Jesus took the twelve again, and began to tell them what things would happen to Him.

Jesus said: Look, we go up to Jerusalem. The Son of Man will be delivered (handed over) to the chief priests, and to the scribes (teachers of the law). They will condemn (judge) Him to death, and will deliver (hand) Him to the Gentiles (people who are not Jews).
They will mock Him, and scourge (whip) Him, and spit on Him, and kill Him. And the third day He will rise again.
James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to Jesus. They said: Master (Teacher), we want You to do for us whatever we desire (ask).
Jesus said to them: What do you want Me to do for you?
They said to Jesus: Grant (allow) us to sit, one on Your right hand, and the other on Your left hand, in Your glory.
But Jesus said to them: You do not know what you ask. Can you drink of the cup that I drink of? And be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?
They said to Jesus: We can. Jesus said to them: You will indeed drink of the cup that I drink of. And with the baptism that I am baptized with, you will be baptized.
But to sit on My right hand and on My left hand is not Mine to give. It will be given to those for whom it is prepared.
When the ten heard it, they began to be much displeased with James and John.

But Jesus called them to Him, and said to them: You know that those who are accounted (thought of as) rulers over the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) exercise lordship (rule as lords) over them. And their great ones exercise authority over them.
But it will not be so among you. Whoever will be great among you will be your minister (servant).
And whoever of you will be the chiefest (first), will be servant of all.
For even the Son of Man came not to be ministered to (served), but to minister (serve), and to give His life a ransom (the price paid to set people free) for many.
They came to Jericho. As Jesus went out of Jericho with His disciples and a great number of people, blind Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, sat by the highway side begging.
When Bartimaeus heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out: Jesus, You Son of David, have mercy on me.
Many charged (told) him to hold his peace (be quiet). But he cried out even more: You Son of David, have mercy on me.
Jesus stood still, and commanded him to be called. They called the blind man, and said to him: Be of good comfort (take heart). Rise (get up). He calls you.
Bartimaeus threw away his garment (coat), rose, and came to Jesus.
Jesus answered him: What do you want Me to do for you? The blind man said to Jesus: Lord, that I might receive my sight.
Jesus said to him: Go your way. Your faith has made you whole (healed). Right away he received his sight, and followed Jesus in the way (road).

11.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. dropping "that cometh in the name of the Lord" in 11:10, and "believe that you have received" for "believe that ye receive" in 11:24, and it added words in 11:23 such as 'God will do it'), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, with generic 'he/his' rendered gender-neutral in v23. V26 is kept (modern Bibles drop it).

verses.text: When they came nigh (near) to Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount of Olives, Jesus sent out two of His disciples.

Jesus said to them: Go your way into the village over against you (in front of you). As soon as you enter into it, you will find a colt (young donkey) tied, that no one has ever sat on. Loose (untie) him, and bring him.
If anyone says to you, Why are you doing this? say that the Lord has need of him. And right away he will send him here.
They went their way, and found the colt (young donkey) tied by the door outside, in a place where two ways (roads) met. And they loosed (untied) him.
Some of those who stood there said to them: What are you doing, loosing (untying) the colt (young donkey)?
They said to them just as Jesus had commanded. And they let them go.
They brought the colt (young donkey) to Jesus, and threw their garments (clothes) on him. And Jesus sat on him.
Many spread their garments (clothes) in the way (road). Others cut down branches off the trees, and strawed (spread) them in the way (road).
Those who went before, and those who followed, cried out: Hosanna (save now)! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!
Blessed be the kingdom of our father David, that comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna (save now) in the highest!
Jesus entered into Jerusalem, and into the temple. When He had looked round about on all things, and now the eventide (evening) had come, He went out to Bethany with the twelve.
On the morrow (next day), when they had come from Bethany, Jesus was hungry.

Seeing a fig tree afar off (in the distance) with leaves, Jesus came to see if haply (perhaps) He might find anything on it. When He came to it, He found nothing but leaves. For the time of figs was not yet.
Jesus answered and said to it: Let no one eat fruit of you hereafter (from now on) for ever. And His disciples heard it.

They came to Jerusalem. Jesus went into the temple, and began to cast out (drive out) those who sold and bought in the temple. He overthrew (turned over) the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of those who sold doves.
Jesus would not suffer (allow) anyone to carry any vessel (container) through the temple.
Jesus taught them: Is it not written: My house will be called of all nations the house of prayer? But you have made it a den of thieves.

The scribes (teachers of the law) and chief priests heard it, and sought (tried to find) how they might destroy Jesus. For they feared Him, because all the people were astonished (amazed) at His doctrine (teaching).
When evening came, Jesus went out of the city.
In the morning, as they passed by, they saw the fig tree dried up from the roots.
Peter, calling to remembrance (remembering), said to Jesus: Master (Teacher), look, the fig tree that You cursed is withered (dried up) away.
Jesus answering said to them: Have faith in God.

For truly I say to you: Whoever says to this mountain, Be removed, and be thrown into the sea, and does not doubt in their heart, but believes that what they say will come to pass (happen), they will have whatever they say.
So I say to you: Whatever things you desire (ask for), when you pray, believe that you receive them, and you will have them.
When you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone. So that your Father who is in heaven may also forgive you your trespasses (wrongs).
But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father who is in heaven forgive your trespasses (wrongs).
They came again to Jerusalem. As Jesus was walking in the temple, the chief priests, and the scribes (teachers of the law), and the elders came to Him.
They said to Him: By what authority do You do these things? And who gave You this authority to do these things?
Jesus answered them: I will also ask you one question. Answer Me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or from men? Answer Me.
They reasoned (talked it over) with themselves. They said: If we say, From heaven, He will say: Why then did you not believe him?
But if we say, From men, they feared the people. For all men counted (believed) John to be a prophet indeed.
They answered Jesus: We cannot tell. And Jesus answering said to them: Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.

12.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. dropping "at him they cast stones" in 12:4, "this is the first commandment" in 12:30, "when they shall rise" in 12:23 and "and with all the soul" in 12:33), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. Parable characters (the man, servants, son) keep their 'he'.

verses.text: Jesus began to speak to them by parables (stories that teach a lesson): A certain man planted a vineyard (grape farm). He set a hedge (fence) around it, and dug a place for the winefat (vat for grape juice), and built a tower. He let it out (rented it) to husbandmen (farmers), and went into a far country.
At the season (harvest time) he sent a servant to the husbandmen (farmers), so that he might receive from the husbandmen (farmers) the fruit of the vineyard (grape farm).
They caught the servant, and beat him, and sent him away empty.
Again he sent another servant to them. At him they threw stones, and wounded him in the head, and sent him away shamefully handled (badly treated).
Again he sent another, and him they killed, and many others. They beat some, and killed some.
So having still one son, his wellbeloved (dearly loved), he sent him also last to them. He said: They will reverence (respect) my son.
But those husbandmen (farmers) said among themselves: This is the heir (the one who will own it all). Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.
They took him, and killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard (grape farm).
So what will the lord (owner) of the vineyard (grape farm) do? He will come and destroy the husbandmen (farmers), and will give the vineyard (grape farm) to others.
Have you not read this scripture: The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner (the most important stone).
This was the Lord's doing, and it is marvellous (wonderful) in our eyes?
They sought (tried) to lay hold on (take hold of) Jesus, but feared the people. For they knew that He had spoken the parable (story) against them. And they left Him, and went their way.
They sent to Jesus some of the Pharisees and of the Herodians (followers of King Herod), to catch Him in His words.

When they came, they said to Him: Master (Teacher), we know that You are true, and care for no one's opinion. For You regard not the person of men (do not favor anyone), but teach the way of God in truth. Is it lawful (allowed by the law) to give tribute (tax) to Caesar, or not?
Should we give, or should we not give? But Jesus, knowing their hypocrisy (pretending), said to them: Why do you tempt (test) Me? Bring Me a penny (a coin worth a day's pay), so I may see it.
They brought it. Jesus said to them: Whose is this image (picture) and superscription (writing)? They said to Him: Caesar's.
Jesus answering said to them: Render (give) to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's. And they marvelled (were amazed) at Him.
Then the Sadducees came to Jesus. They say there is no resurrection (rising from the dead). They asked Him:
Master (Teacher), Moses wrote to us: If a man's brother dies, and leaves his wife behind him, and leaves no children, his brother should take his wife, and raise up seed (children) for his brother.
Now there were seven brethren (brothers). The first took a wife, and dying left no seed (children).
The second took her, and died, and he did not leave any seed (children) either. And the third did the same.
All seven had her, and left no seed (children). Last of all the woman died also.
So in the resurrection (rising from the dead), when they rise, whose wife will she be of them? For all seven had her as wife.
Jesus answering said to them: Do you not err (are you not wrong) because of this, because you do not know the scriptures, or the power of God?
For when they rise from the dead, they do not marry, and are not given in marriage. But they are like the angels who are in heaven.
And about the dead, that they rise: Have you not read in the book of Moses, how God spoke to him in the bush? God said: I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
He is not the God of the dead, but the God of the living. So you do greatly err (are badly wrong).

One of the scribes (teachers of the law) came. He had heard them reasoning (talking) together, and perceived (saw) that Jesus had answered them well. He asked Jesus: Which is the first commandment of all?
Jesus answered him: The first of all the commandments is: Hear, O Israel. The Lord our God is one Lord.
And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength. This is the first commandment.
And the second is like it, namely this: You shall love your neighbour as yourself. There is no other commandment greater than these.
The scribe (teacher of the law) said to Jesus: Well, Master (Teacher), You have said the truth. For there is one God, and there is none other but He.

And to love Him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love one's neighbour as oneself, is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.
When Jesus saw that he answered discreetly (wisely), He said to him: You are not far from the kingdom of God. And after that no one durst (dared) ask Him any question.
While Jesus taught in the temple, He answered: How do the scribes (teachers of the law) say that Christ is the son of David?
For David himself said by the Holy Spirit: The LORD said to my Lord: Sit on My right hand, until I make Your enemies Your footstool (a place to rest Your feet).
So David himself calls Him Lord. How then is He his son? And the common people heard Him gladly.
Jesus said to them in His doctrine (teaching): Beware of the scribes (teachers of the law), who love to go around in long clothing, and love salutations (greetings) in the marketplaces,
And the chief (best) seats in the synagogues (meeting houses), and the uppermost rooms (best places) at feasts.
They devour (eat up) widows' houses, and for a pretence (to look good) make long prayers. These will receive greater damnation (punishment).
Jesus sat over against (across from) the treasury (temple money box), and beheld (watched) how the people threw money into the treasury (temple money box). And many who were rich threw in much.
A certain poor widow came, and she threw in two mites (tiny coins), which make a farthing (smallest coin).
Jesus called His disciples to Him, and said to them: Truly I say to you: This poor widow has thrown in more than all those who have thrown into the treasury (temple money box).
For they all threw in of their abundance (extra). But she of her want (need) threw in all that she had, even all her living (what she had to live on).

13.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase that followed the modern Greek text, e.g. dropping "and troubles" in 13:8, "neither do ye premeditate" in 13:11, "spoken of by Daniel the prophet" in 13:14, and "and pray" in 13:33), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, with generic 'he/his' rendered gender-neutral in v13, v14-16. The parable of the watchful owner (v34-36) keeps its pronouns.

verses.text: As Jesus went out of the temple, one of His disciples said to Him: Master (Teacher), see what kind of stones and what buildings are here!
Jesus answering said to him: Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone will be left on another, that will not be thrown down.
As Jesus sat on the mount of Olives over against (across from) the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked Him privately:
Tell us, when will these things be? And what will be the sign when all these things will be fulfilled (come true)?
Jesus answering them began to say: Take heed (be careful) that no one deceives (fools) you.
For many will come in My name, saying, I am Christ. And they will deceive (fool) many.
When you hear of wars and rumours (reports) of wars, do not be troubled. For such things must happen. But the end will not be yet.

For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in divers (many different) places, and there will be famines (times of no food) and troubles. These are the beginnings of sorrows (great pains).

But take heed (be careful) to yourselves. For they will deliver you up (hand you over) to councils (courts). In the synagogues (meeting houses) you will be beaten. And you will be brought before rulers and kings for My sake, for a testimony (proof) against them.
And the gospel (good news) must first be published (preached) among all nations.

But when they lead you, and deliver you up (hand you over), take no thought (do not worry) beforehand what you will speak, and do not premeditate (plan it ahead). But whatever is given to you in that hour, speak that. For it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.
Now the brother will betray (hand over) the brother to death, and the father the son. Children will rise up against their parents, and cause them to be put to death.
You will be hated by all men for My name's sake. But whoever endures (keeps on faithful) to the end, that person will be saved.

But when you see the abomination of desolation (the hateful thing that brings ruin), spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not (let whoever reads understand), then let those who are in Judaea flee (run away) to the mountains.
Let whoever is on the housetop not go down into the house, or enter in, to take anything out of their house.
Let whoever is in the field not turn back again to take up their garment (coat).
But woe (great trouble) to those who are with child (pregnant), and to those who give suck (nurse babies) in those days!
Pray that your flight (escape) is not in the winter.
For in those days there will be affliction (trouble), such as was not from the beginning of the creation which God created to this time, and never will be.
Unless the Lord had shortened those days, no flesh (person) would be saved. But for the elect's (chosen people's) sake, whom He has chosen, He has shortened the days.
Then if anyone says to you, Lo (look), here is Christ, or, Lo (look), He is there, do not believe it.
For false Christs and false prophets will rise. They will show signs and wonders, to seduce (lead astray), if it were possible, even the elect (chosen people).
But take heed (be careful). Look, I have foretold (told ahead of time) you all things.
But in those days, after that tribulation (trouble), the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give her light.
The stars of heaven will fall, and the powers that are in heaven will be shaken.
Then they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds with great power and glory.
Then He will send His angels. They will gather together His elect (chosen people) from the four winds, from the uttermost (farthest) part of the earth to the uttermost (farthest) part of heaven.
Now learn a parable (story that teaches a lesson) of the fig tree. When her branch is still tender (soft), and puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.
In the same way, when you see these things come to pass (happen), know that it is nigh (near), even at the doors.
Truly I say to you: This generation will not pass, until all these things are done.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will not pass away.
But of that day and that hour no one knows, no, not the angels who are in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father.
Take heed (be careful), watch and pray. For you do not know when the time is.
For the Son of Man is like a man taking a far journey. He left his house, and gave authority to his servants, and to every man his work, and commanded the porter (doorkeeper) to watch.
So watch. For you do not know when the master of the house comes: at evening, or at midnight, or at the cockcrowing (when the rooster crows), or in the morning.
Otherwise, coming suddenly, he may find you sleeping.
And what I say to you I say to all: Watch.
